show: 1929. Three predictions. Which one aged best?
say: Nineteen twenty-nine. Three predictions. Which one aged best?

show: A. Irving Fisher: "Stock prices have reached what looks like a permanently high plateau."
say: A. Irving Fisher. Stock prices have reached what looks like a permanently high plateau.

show: B. Roger Babson: "Sooner or later a crash is coming."
say: B. Roger Babson. Sooner or later, a crash is coming.

show: C. John Raskob: "Everybody ought to be rich." Put $15 a month into stocks.
say: C. John Raskob. Everybody ought to be rich. Put fifteen dollars a month into stocks.

show: Two weeks later: Black Tuesday. Fisher loses his fortune.
say: Two weeks later: Black Tuesday. Fisher loses his fortune.

show: The Raskob plan, kept up through the Depression, turned about $3,700 into almost $10,000 by 1949.
say: The Raskob plan, kept up through the Depression, turned about thirty-seven hundred dollars into almost ten thousand, by nineteen forty-nine.

show: No forecast needed. A fund of your own should start at $10.
say: No forecast needed. A fund of your own should start at ten dollars.

show: Who Called It, part 1. Next: Dow 36,000.
say: Who Called It, part one. Next: Dow thirty-six thousand.
